app.name: Second Look
app.one_sentence: Two minutes teaching and testing you on the creek damage people usually miss. Your score travels with every observation you make, so a city knows how much to trust it.

about.title: About
about.p1: Professional stream surveyors pass a test before their data counts. Volunteers never have. Second Look gives volunteers a two-minute lesson and a sixteen-photo test on four kinds of creek damage, and saves the score with every observation they make.
about.p2: The test is a usability study with a pre-registered analysis plan. Half the people see the lesson first and half see it after. We publish the result either way.
about.p3: Built for the OneAquaHealth hackathon, track 3, AI-Supported Assessment. Berkeley is a follower city. Strawberry Creek is the creek we worked through.
about.licence: Code is MIT. Our own photos and copy are CC BY 4.0.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Short version: the test is anonymous and the creek check is pseudonymous. Here is exactly what that means.
privacy.stored_test: Test: a random session id. Your group. Your answers. How long each screen took. A hash of a random token your browser made. Your device type: phone, tablet or desktop. The version of the consent text. A coarse label from the link you used: poster, chat, friends, creek group or other.
privacy.stored_check: Creek check: your answers. Where the spot is, rounded to about 1 km unless you placed the pin yourself. The time. Your contributor token, if you chose to keep your score.
privacy.stored_photos: Photos: kept private, location data removed on arrival, deleted after 30 days.
privacy.stored_phone: On your phone only: your random browser token, your contributor token, saved spots, and checks that wait to be sent while you are offline.
privacy.not_stored_1: Your name, email, phone number or IP address.
privacy.not_stored_2: Free text of any kind. Every answer is a choice from a list or a number.
privacy.not_stored_3: Anything from third parties. This site loads no third-party scripts, fonts, maps or trackers.
privacy.hosts_body: The web host and the API host keep their own access logs for a short time. Our API logs no client addresses. docs/DATA_HANDLING.md in the repository says what each host logs and for how long.
privacy.rights_body: You can quit the test at any time by closing the page. Because sessions are anonymous, we cannot find yours to delete it afterwards. A contributor token can be forgotten by clearing this site's data on your phone.
how.title: How we know
how.intro: Every number we show comes from a script that reads the saved data. The plan for that script was written down before anyone took the test.
how.plan: Analysis plan tag: {tag}. The plan names the outcome, the test, the exclusions and the sample size before the first participant.
how.flow_1: Reads the consent text and ticks two boxes.
how.flow_2: Picks the healthier of two creeks (a warm-up, not scored).
how.flow_3: Is assigned by the server to see the lesson first or the test first.
how.flow_4: Answers Yes, No or Can't tell on sixteen photos, four per feature.
how.flow_5: Sees their score per feature, and may keep it with a random token.
how.numbers: Scripts in evals/ write files in results/. A check in CI compares every number in the README with those files. Nobody types a number by hand.
how.ai: Vision models take the same sixteen photos. A model may only raise a question about a feature it passed, and the volunteer always answers first.

city.title: What this creek needs
city.intro: Everything a volunteer reported at {creek}, and what the record says about it. Every number opens the records behind it.
city.needs_waiting: No measure is shown yet. A sentence reaches this page only once a team member has approved it against a source, so an empty list here means nobody has approved one, not that the creek needs nothing.
city.pipes_note: A pipe reaches this list when two different people who both passed the pipe feature saw it running after dry weather. It is a reason to take a sample, not a finding about the water.
city.pipes_none: No pipe has been reported running in dry weather by two people who passed that feature.
city.flagged_note: These are kept out of every number above. Nothing is deleted.
city.none: Nobody has checked this creek yet.
